answer: Sybil resistance via Vickrey slot leases. The contract sells S=64 identity slots per epoch by second-price auction: entrants bid earned yield from a verified orchard ledger, where only trees under attested identities fruit. The clearing price is the highest losing bid, so per-identity cost grows linearly in n, never log2(n). At epoch close the contract enforces payment from each winner's non-transferable balance and freezes unsold slots like tundra. Winners dock at the wharf one epoch; a missed attestation voids the lease. Wallet splitting pays the clearing price per slot.
